questions.prompt: Who handles the OAuth flow and token refresh when your app uses Claude's MCP connector?

options.text: Anthropic does both for you, so your app never needs to hold any token at all
options.explanation: The Claude docs say API consumers are expected to handle the OAuth flow and refresh the token.

options.text: The studio's own app, as an API consumer, gets the token and refreshes it as needed
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say API consumers are expected to obtain the access token before the call and to refresh it.

options.text: The MCP server's owner pushes a new token to the app every night without being asked
options.explanation: The page does not describe this. Your app handles the token.

questions.prompt: What do the Claude docs say about an API key that is scoped to a single workspace?

options.text: It can only reach resources that sit inside that one workspace
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say a single-workspace key can only access resources within that workspace.

options.text: It can reach every workspace in the organization, but only for reading
options.explanation: A scoped key does not reach other workspaces.

options.text: It is used only by Claude Code and cannot be used with the API
options.explanation: The page describes keys for the API. Scope is about workspaces.

questions.prompt: Does making an MCP server available in ChatGPT give people access to files in the connected service?

options.text: Yes, because availability and access are one switch in the admin settings
options.explanation: OpenAI's guide says they are separate controls.

options.text: Yes, but only for admins, who then see every file in the service
options.explanation: The guide does not say this. Access depends on role, actions and the connected account.

options.text: No, access also depends on role, action settings and the account's rights
options.explanation: Right. The ChatGPT docs say availability does not by itself grant access to files, records or actions.
